_doc: GBD dating cabinet = DATA only (cabinet #6, built 2026-07-16 following control/CABINET_METHOD.md). GBD dates by CONVERGENCE of: COM-stamp wording (linear 'London England' pre-merger vs round 'Made in London England' post-1981) + stem rondelle generations (metal vs painted) + line/grade years + French-vs-English production marks. THE CLIFF = the 1981 merger with Comoy's (single Cadogan factory since). SOURCES (local-first): pipedia mirror staging/pipedia/GBD.json (history + G.L. Pease dating post, 1996) + pipephil mirror logos/en/logo-gbd.html (corroborates rondelle + linear-stamp rules). DISAGREEMENT noted: pipephil says Cadogan took over 'sometime in the 1970s'; pipedia says the GBD-Comoy's production merger = 1981 -- the STAMP/rondelle cliff is tied to the 1981 merger (both sources) and that is what is encoded. HALLMARKED silver bands date exactly (Birmingham/London) -- channel waits for generic.json UK charts; note pipephil's 1913-vs-1938 'o'/'O' example: same escutcheon, honest ambiguity.

history_anchors._doc: 1850 founded in PARIS (Ganneval, Bondier & Donninger -- meerschaum first, briar early). Company names over time: Ganneval Bondier & Donninger -> Bondier Ulrich & Cie -> Bine Marechal & Cie -> A. Marechal Ruchon & Cie. 1902 sold to A. Oppenheimer & Co (London); London factory opens 1903; Saint-Claude plant (Sina + Verguet merger) operating 1906. Dual production LONDON + PARIS between the wars (London dominant from WWI). 1920s: Cadogan Investments holding formed over Oppenheimer's brands (BBB 1920, Loewe, Comoy's shares). 1952: the Paris factory MOVES to Saint-Claude. 1981: GBD merges with Comoy's -- one English factory for both = the collector cliff (pre-1981 = the good era; Smokers' Haven was the main US supplier until the early 1980s). SECONDS (own rules -- do NOT date by this cabinet's lines): Beau Nash, Brentwood, City Gold Star, Country Club, Digby, Irwin's, Peter Kent, Samuel Pepys, Theydon, Town Club, Jameson's (pipephil/pipedia); SEPARATE brands from the same house: Dr. Plumb's (1925, France/Canada market), Peter Piper, Marcee (French market). HONESTY WARNING from pipedia itself: Saint-Claude-made sub-brand pipes were routinely stamped 'London made'/'London England' -- COM wording on cheap lines is not fully trustworthy. FAMILY LINE FACT (BNA primary, 2026-07-17): CITY DE LUXE = Oppenheimer house line LAUNCHED July 1921 (national campaign, 60-years-of-pipemaking, 101 shapes, push-in stem, 5/6; Bystander ad signed OPPENHEIMER'S PIPES WITH A PEDIGREE; 38 Finsbury Square) -> any City de Luxe pipe = floor 1921; still retailed 1931 (5/6) and Dec 1939. See brand_research/gbd_dating/bna_city_de_luxe_facts.md. GBD-Unique note: 'GBD Unique' has ZERO hits in all of BNA (2026-07-17) -> the 1940-vs-1965 mystery stays on US-paper evidence.

brand_marks.physical: GBD-in-oval shank stamp (International/Himalaya also used a rounded-rectangle variant). Stem rondelle = inserted metal plate with GBD initials, introduced from Paris in the late 1920s; discontinued after the 1981 merger; late pipes got a PAINTED rondelle; brass rondelles REAPPEARED on recent Cadogan production. City de Luxe (1921) wore an inserted STAR on the stem.

table.note: the ROUND Comoy-style stamp replaced GBD's linear stamp after the 1981 merger (G.L. Pease)

linear 'London England' = pre-merger English GBD (pipephil: 'prior to this time... stamped London England in a straight line, even if sometimes crafted in France' -- so England wording, French wood possible)
'London Made' became 'Standard London Made' after WWI as a LINE name; also appears alongside 'London. England' on later pipes (pipephil International example) -> wide, low-conf
Oppenheimer's Saint-Claude plant ran from 1906; French GBD production ends with the 1981 single-factory merger
the Paris factory moved to Saint-Claude in 1952

line_years._notes: xtra: one of the earliest named models (late 19th c, start approx 1895 flagged); 'Xtras haven't been made since the 1930's... discontinued 1937' (Pease + pipedia editor). pedigree: sketched ~1926 but 'not produced until the later 1930s' -> FLOOR 1936; no documented end. new era: existed by 1931 ('in 1931 the top model') -> floor 1925 approx. prehistoric: 'entirely new' in the interwar paragraph -> floor 1930 approx. extra dry: metal-filter line introduced late 1920s in France -> floor 1927 approx. city de luxe: introduced 1921 (star stem inlay); pipephil lists it under SECONDS -> floor only. marcee: French-market brand offered until WWII + 1-2 years after -> [1902,1947] low. riseagle: Paris-made 1-Shilling line killed by the post-war excise tax -> [1920,1947] low approx. collector + unique: introduced late 1960s-late 1970s (Horry Jamieson freehands) -> [1965,1985] approx. century: 'first introduced some time in the 1960s or 1970s as I recall' (Pease, scant literature) -> FLOOR 1960 low. autumn gold/bermuda/facet: post-merger Cadogan lines. NOT encoded (thin): Camelia ('only around for a few years', London 2.5-Shilling interwar), Pub + CW churchwarden (names too short/generic to match safely -- confirm-flow), New Standard (1930s intro approx but 'standard' matches too much), Tanganyika meerschaum collab (1970s, note only), International/Universe/Speciale/Granitan/Sauvage/Sierra/Legacy/Concorde/Virgin/Prestige/Varichrome/Bronze Velvet/Straight Grain/Prodigy/Jubilee/Tapestry/Ebony (grade list exists but no intro years documented).

table.label: painted (not inlaid) GBD rondelle = post-merger (Pease: 'you can be assured... late-model, made after the merge')
inlaid SILVER rondelle = late 1920s until the 1981 merger

metal rondelle: introduced late 1920s, discontinued after the 1981 merger BUT brass rondelles reappeared on recent Cadogan production (sources disagree on finality) -> weak pre-1981 hint only. NOTE: bare 'rondelle' deliberately NOT matched (could be the painted kind -> confirm-flow)

stamped_year._doc: Commemoratives carry literal years (150 Year Celebration billiard ~2000). Generic channel reads the last 4-digit year.

channels_future.assay_hallmark: Silver-banded GBDs hallmarked Birmingham/London -> EXACT year once generic.json UK date-letter charts land. Encode pipephil's caution: Birmingham lower-case 'o' (1913) vs capital 'O' (1938) share the same escutcheon -> honest ambiguity, offer both candidates.
channels_future.shape_chart: GBD shape numbers exist (4-digit, e.g. 9242 bent Rhodesian; 'GBD Shapes/Numbers' pipedia page is in the mirror) -- no design-year chart yet; Pease: shapes changed almost yearly, so old catalogs could bracket a pipe. Future enrichment.
